subject: Civil Engineering
title: Flexible Pavements: Asphalt Roads
description: Learn Flexible Pavements: Asphalt Roads in one minute.

hook.text: Asphalt covers 94% of paved roads in the United States. It's the world's road surface.

buildup.text: Flexible pavements bend under load. Layers of asphalt, base, and subbase spread the force.

discovery.text: Asphalt is aggregate glued together with bitumen — a petroleum product. It's recyclable.

twist.text: Hot-mix asphalt is placed at 300°F. Warm-mix uses lower temperatures to save energy.

climax.text: Perpetual pavements are designed to last 50+ years — deep layers never crack.

punchline.text: Asphalt bends, heals, and recycles. That's why it covers the world.

quiz.question: Why are asphalt pavements called 'flexible'?
options: They can be easily removed and replaced overnight
They bend slightly under traffic loads and distribute force through layers
They change color with temperature to warn drivers of ice
